title: CHRISTIAN LIBERTY
mv: Therefore my people are gone into captivity, because they have no knowledge: and their honourable men are famished, and their multitude dried up with thirst.
mvp: “Therefore my people are gone into captivity, because they have no knowledge: and their honourable men are famished, and their multitude dried up with thirst.” Isaiah 5:13
assignment: Identify five (5) areas some believers are still living as though they are in bondage despite Christ’s freedom (2X5=10 marks).

b.x: Christian liberty is freedom from sin and the law through faith in Jesus Christ. This enables believers to serve God willingly without fear of condemnation. It is not a license to sin but a freedom from guilt (John 8:36), the penalty of sin and the obligation to earn salvation through works. This lesson will reveal the causes of bondage we were liberated from and how to live in the reality of our liberty.

i: Sin: It enslaves and separates us from God (John 8:34; Isaiah 59:1-2). Anyone who deliberately sins and makes it a lifestyle is in bondage (Romans 6:16).
Ignorance of God’s word: Lack of knowledge keeps people in spiritual darkness (Hosea 4:6; Isaiah 5:13).
Demonic oppression: Being influenced or controlled by demonic forces (2 Corinthians 4:4; Ephesians 6:12).
Legalism and Religious Bondage: Being bound by the traditions of men rather than God’s leading (Colossians 2:8).
Fear: It can imprison the heart (Romans 8:15).
Addictions and Fleshly Desires: Being trapped in lust, consistent negative thoughts and worldly behaviours (2 Corinthians 10:4-5; 2 Peter 2:19).

b.x: Regardless of the cause of the bondage, God has promised to deliver even “the lawful captives” (Isaiah 49:24-25). True and total freedom comes only through Christ (John 8:36). His death and resurrection broke the power of sin (Romans 8:2). It is expedient that believers in Christ genuinely repent from dead works (Acts 3:19); live by the Holy Spirit (2 Corinthians 3:17; Galatians 5:16-18); study and obey God’s word (Romans 6:16); pray and faithfully serve the Lord to the end (Matthew 26:41; Romans 6:16).

In addition, believers must consciously live in the truth and reality of their liberty in Christ (John 8:31-32). The Truth is that Jesus did not just declare our freedom; He bought the freedom by substituting Himself for us. For instance:

i: He was wounded and bruised for our transgression (Isaiah 53:5a, 1 Peter 2:22, 24a).
He was beaten for our healing (Isaiah 53:5b; 1 Peter 2:24b).
He became poor for us to be rich (2 Corinthians 8:9).
He accepted false accusation and condemnation, so that we will not be condemned by the enemy (Romans 8:1-2, 33-34).
He became a curse by hanging on the tree to remove every curse hanging on our lives (Galatians 3:13-14).
He died and rose, to give us victory over death (1 Corinthians 15:55-57).
He went to hell and seized the key so that we will not go there (Revelation 1:18).

b.x: Hence, believers are admonished in Galatians 5:1 to “Stand fast therefore in the liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free, and be not entangled again with the yoke of bondage.”
Every believer should identify and break chains of bondage through Christ and reaffirm their freedom in Him as a daily choice and walk.

i: Mention four instances in which Jesus bought our freedom by substituting Himself for us.
